quote:
In total 32 participants (recruited via the local Sona system from Ghent University) completed the experiment between March and July 2023 and remained in the final analysis ... For the proximity effect, we conducted three univariate ANOVAs: one ANOVA compared schedules on which participants got blocked in the first trial (i.e., 1/1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4). ... Table 1. The F values and p values from the ANOVAs on the effects of proximity and effort across 4, 3, and 2 trials. ... confirm RT ... Proximity effect ... 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 1/1 ... 1.78 (
p
= 0.156)
reason: Methods explicitly establishes a balanced within-participant design with final N = 32 (after replacing excluded participants) analyzed via uncorrected univariate repeated-measures ANOVAs in R package ez across k = 4, 3, and 2 within-person schedule conditions (yielding df = (k - 1, (k - 1)(N - 1)) = (3, 93), (2, 62), and (1, 31)), corroborated by every exact p-value in Table 1 (here F(3, 93) = 1.78 gives p = 0.1564, whereas shipped F(3, 28) = 1.78 erroneously uses N - 4 = 28 and gives p = 0.174; the only discordant pair in Table 1, effort/surprise F = 5.39 with p < 0.001 in row 318, is an internal primary-article p-reporting error where F(3, 93) = 5.39 yields p = 0.00183, rather than evidence for a different df model). Reconciling v1 and prior_adjudication (which omitted df), positive design, count, and p-value evidence uniquely establishes F(3, 93) = 1.78.
